title: Congratulations, Puerto Rico: You Mastered Medicare Advantage Five-Star Ratings, and CMS Mastered Paying You Like a Two-Star Failure.
description: CMS rewrote the Medicare Advantage test for 2027. Of the 508 contracts rated, the enrollment-weighted average fell to 3.99 stars, only about 37% of plans reached four stars or better, and just 15 plans in the country earned a perfect five, down from 22. New measures track patients prescribed opioids and benzodiazepines at the same time and older adults on several anticholinergic drugs, and the weight of the measures that track whether members actually get or stay healthier was tripled. Fourteen of the fifteen perfect plans are for-profit, and two of them are in Puerto Rico. MCS Classicare earned five stars for the fourth year in a row with 360,519 members; Triple-S Advantage earned five stars on its HMO contract with 120,943 members. Those two contracts cover more than 481,000 people, more five-star Medicare Advantage patients than all the mainland five-star plans combined, about 305,000. The island did it with benchmark payments far below the states, and its leaders credit alliances with physicians and community organizations rather than software: community health workers at the kitchen table, looking at the pill bottles, instead of an automated text nobody reads. The closing question: if a jurisdiction with the lowest funding in the system can put half a million people in five-star care, what is the mainland's excuse?
short_title: Congratulations, Puerto Rico: You Mastered Five-Star Ratings. CMS Mastered Two-Star Pay.
